text:
alice: thinking out loud — proposing a compact UX for automatic fallback escalation that is quota-aware and audit-friendly. want to avoid a giant policy editor, focus on: soft vs hard degrade, escalation windows, and a preview/simulate step. thoughts?

ben: +1 on preview. we need to surface token-cost delta and latency impact before enabling. also: who gets paged when auto-fallback triggers?

carla: paging should be optional. default -> alert only to on-call if it's a hard degrade (errors). soft degrade (e.g., 10% sample redirect) => just telemetry.

dan: what about rate limits? if fallback increases token usage it could blow through quotas. UI should show projected quota burn for 1h/24h given current traffic.

alice: exactly. idea: policy presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with a quick toggle. presets populate three knobs: trigger threshold, sample rate, escalation action.

eva: can we add a tiny inline simulation button that runs against recent traffic window? e.g., "Run against last 30m" and show how many sessions would have fallen back and cost delta.

ben: simulation is great. must be privacy-safe (redact prompts). also include failure reason buckets: model_error, rate_limit, latency_p95, token_budget_exhausted.

carla: for audit, every automatic fallback event should be recorded with: policy_id, reason_code, affected_route, original_model, fallback_model, decision_trace_id. exportable as CSV/JSON. retention default 90 days + enterprise 365.

alice: agreed. UI wiring: when you open a rollout (route -> model rollout -> fallback), top banner: current preset, last simulated run, last real trigger times. quick actions: disable automatic fallback, set to preview-only, enable auto-escalate to on-call.

dan: one API/implementation question — should auto-fallback be a field on the route object (e.g., route.auto_fallback = {...}) or a separate routing-policy resource that routes reference? pros/cons?

ben: separate resource allows reuse across routes and easier rollout changes. but it's more objects for users to manage. putting it on route is simpler UX for small teams.

carla: leaning toward a routing-policy resource in the API, but console should surface it as an inline editor for the common case, with a link to the underlying policy for advanced edits.

alice: nice compromise. console mock: a small card in the rollout panel with current policy name, a slider for severity (soft -> hard), sample rate input, triggers dropdown (errors, p95, token budget), and a "Simulate" button. a link "View policy JSON" for power users.

eva: sample UI snippet for the card:```
Fallback policy: Balanced (editable)
Severity: [---o-----]  (soft -> hard)
Triggers: [latency_p95, model_error]
Sample rate: 10%
[Simulate] [Enable auto-fallback (preview only)]
```

ben: need to define exact telemetry to emit on triggers: event.fallback.trigger, event.fallback.decision_trace, event.fallback.simulation_result, event.fallback.cost_estimate. Add labels: team, route, policy_id, severity, sample_rate.

carla: and correlate with request traces. include a small trace_id in the event so we can playback the request path in the trace system. we should also expose a replay endpoint that can re-run the sample in a sandbox for forensic.

dan: replay endpoint ok, but ensure rate limits and safe execution (no external calls). annotate replays with a special header and store them as simulation-only unless user explicitly replays against production model.

alice: ops-bot note: "auto-fallback policy deployed to staging" whenever a new policy is toggled to enable in non-preview mode. we should tag that in audit logs.

ops-bot: auto-fallback policy "balanced-v2" enabled in staging by alice at 2024-06-12T14:22Z :white_check_mark:

ben: small API example for the routing-policy resource for review:```json
{
  "id": "pol-1234",
  "name": "balanced",
  "triggers": ["latency_p95", "model_error"],
  "severity": "soft",
  "sample_rate": 0.1,
  "escalation": {"mode": "none", "on_call": false}
}
```

carla: add an audit field for created_by/created_at and a "preview_runs" array that stores last N simulation summaries (no raw prompts).

eva: UX edge-case: if a policy references a fallback model that's incompatible (e.g., different tokenizer), console should validate and warn. maybe a compatibility check at save time.

alice: good catch. also we need a fallback health score heuristic — if fallback model is returning < 80% of expected quality on eval prompts, block auto-fallback unless user overrides. show that score in the card.

ben: will add telemetry requirement: fallback.quality_eval_score and sample_evals_count. blockers: need a fast offline eval runner or cached recent evals.

dan: ops question: can we support multi-step escalation? e.g., 1) soft sample redirect, 2) after N triggers escalate to 50% redirect, 3) then full redirect or throttle. UI should let you author a simple linear escalation plan.

alice: yes — show a timeline UI: step 0: preview -> step 1: 10% for 5m -> step 2: 50% for 10m -> step 3: full. each step with an "if x% errors persist" condition.

carla: store escalation history in audit so we can reconstruct what happened when a customer saw degradation. link to traces and simulation runs.

eva: final note: include a lightweight changelog UI for policies with diff view between versions. "Revert" button to roll back to previous policy quickly.

alice: cool. next actions: ben to sketch telemetry events, carla to propose audit schema & retention, dan to validate replay safety constraints, eva to prototype the card UI. I'll assemble a mock screenshot and small copy for the console team.

ben: on it. starting a doc in /designs/rollouts/autofallback-telemetry.md

carla: I'll ping legal on retention policy.

dan: will run a quick tech spike on replay sandbox later today.

alice: thanks all :rocket:
